ground_truth: Final confirmed diagnosis: Infiltrative hepatic angiosarcoma. The presentation was misleading because the clinical picture (ascites with a high serum-ascites albumin gradient indicating portal hypertension, splenomegaly, cytopenias, cholestatic liver chemistries) strongly mimicked decompensated cirrhosis, yet the patient had no cirrhosis risk factors and an exhaustive workup for infectious (Coxiella, Bartonella, Brucella), viral (hepatitis A/B/D), metabolic/genetic (alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, hemochromatosis), autoimmune, and vascular (Budd-Chiari) causes was negative; ascitic cytology was negative and bone marrow aspirate/flow cytometry were unrevealing. The key discriminator was the diffuse INFILTRATIVE pattern (no discrete liver masses), splenic lesions on CT, and FDG uptake in liver, spleen, and bone marrow on PET-CT. CONFIRMED by liver biopsy: atypical spindle-cell proliferation with hyperchromatic nuclei and scant pale eosinophilic cytoplasm growing along the hepatic sinusoids, with nuclear positivity for the endothelial marker ERG on immunohistochemistry (vascular/endothelial malignancy). Correct disposition: this is an aggressive, near-uniformly fatal malignancy; given advanced age and comorbidities the appropriate course was a goals-of-care discussion. The family elected comfort/palliative care and the patient died a few weeks later. Teaching point: cirrhosis-mimi
judge_rationale:
GROUND TRUTH: The confirmed diagnosis is infiltrative hepatic ANGIOSARCOMA — a vascular/endothelial malignancy (ERG+ spindle cells along hepatic sinusoids), NOT a hematolymphoid neoplasm. Neither output names angiosarcoma. So neither nails the specific entity. The discriminating question for judging is therefore: (a) how well each captures the correct FRAMING (an infiltrative, non-cirrhotic, sinusoidal malignancy requiring tissue diagnosis), (b) how appropriate the recommended confirmatory step is (liver biopsy — the actual confirmatory test), and (c) calibration — is the confidence proportionate to the fact that the leading specific guess (lymphoma) is WRONG.

SHARED CORRECTNESS: Both correctly identify the meta-level framing the ground truth emphasizes — non-cirrhotic portal hypertension from a diffuse INFILTRATIVE process, with the negative cirrhosis workup, splenic lesions, and tri-compartment FDG avidity as the discriminators. Both correctly drive toward tissue biopsy as the decisive next step, which matches the ground truth's confirmatory move (liver biopsy). Both correctly note that negative marrow aspirate/flow and negative cytology do NOT exclude infiltrative malignancy. This framing is the most transferable teaching point, and both get it.

SHARED ERROR: Both anchor on hepatosplenic/intravascular LYMPHOMA as the single best specific diagnosis. This is wrong vs ground truth (angiosarcoma, a vascular sarcoma).
